This message comes from Kachava. A little boost goes a long way, especially when it comes to caring for your gut during the holiday season and beyond.
Introducing Kachava's new 3-in-1 digestive boost. Simply mix into your favorite Kachava shake or any cold beverage.
Go to kachava.com and use code NPR for 15% off your first order. That's K-A-C-H-A-V-A.com. Code NPR.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Dan Rowan.
Trump administration officials say no one was in danger as the FAA called for a full ground stop.
For the first time since 9/11, more than 3,000 planes were in the air when the FAA experienced instability in the radar and communication systems.
NPR's Deepa Shivaram reports.
Department of Homeland Security Secretary Mark Wayne Mullen briefed reporters at the White House after the ground stop was lifted.
The public was never at danger through this process. There was never any lives at risk. There was no flights at risk. FAA was able to handle it.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy also briefed reporters. He says the FAA switches got overloaded with data, became inconsistent, and because of that, they shut the system down.
The secretary says Congress needs to fund a package that would help the FAA with new technology. He added that he "didn't anticipate we would have an outage like this."
In the meantime, Duffy says a ground stop like this could happen again with the old technology in place.
Deepa Shivaram, NPR News, the White House.
Democrats say they have a mandate to deliver change when they take control of Congress next year.
But there are divides over how far that change should go and who should lead it.
As NPR's Elena Moore reports, the debate is now playing out in the Senate where minority leader Chuck Schumer faces a challenge from fellow Democrat Chris Van Hollen for the top job next year.
Van Hollen has represented Maryland and the Senate since 2017 and leans more progressive.
He announced his intention to challenge Schumer Thursday night and says the midterm showed how much voters want Democrats to reject the status quo.
It comes as Schumer has faced questions about his leadership in recent years and a handful of incoming soon to be senators have declined to support him.
But despite that, Van Hollen acknowledges he's an underdog in this race and Schumer has said he has the needed votes to win.
The race will ultimately be decided in early December when the caucus votes.
Elena Moore, NPR News.
SpaceX has conducted another launch of its giant Starship rocket, as NPR's Jeff Braunfield reports the company has a lot riding on the mission.
The SpaceX rocket lifted off from its launch pad in South Texas.
Starship had a smooth ride to orbit, but its massive super heavy booster rocket did not make the trip back to Earth as planned.
Rather than landing back at the launch site, it crashed into the Gulf.
Starship, meanwhile, went on to deploy 26 satellites for SpaceX's Starlink constellation.
If all goes well, it will return to the launch site Saturday, where we'll land at the pad.
That landing would be a key step towards making the rocket more rapidly reusable.
Jeff Brumfield, NPR News.
On Wall Street, stocks close mixed Friday, two in the week.
The Dow added 50 points, but the NASDAQ and the S&P had losses.
This is NPR News.
President Trump says leaders of the U.S., China, and Russia will meet next Thursday at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Summit in China to discuss several worldwide issues.
Senior U.S. officials say Trump does plan to discuss the U.S. war with Iran in reaching a three-day agreement on the nuclear stockpiles.
However, it is not expected they will discuss Russia's war against Ukraine.
In Turkey, almost 200 nations are discussing how to limit emissions from fossil fuels now that their current climate global is out of reach.
NPR's Lauren Summer reports.
It was 11 years ago now that countries agreed on a goal to stave off the most intense impacts of climate change.
Warming would be limited to 1.5 degrees Celsius, which is 2.7 degrees Fahrenheit.
Now that goal is out of reach.
The planet has almost reached that level of warming, and countries continue to burn fossil fuels.
Discussions at the COP 31 climate summit are now focused on how much hotter it will get, which affects extreme weather around the planet.
Despite the U.S. being one of the largest producers of greenhouse gas emissions, the Trump administration is not participating in the talks.
Lauren Summer, NPR News.
Pope Leo is back in his former dioceses in Peru as he continues his Latin American trip, telling Catholics it's a joy to return.
The Vatican estimates that one million people lined the Pope's motorcade, and another half million were at a mass he later served for where he served as a missionary priest and bishop.
I'm Dan Ronan, NPR News in Washington.
